title: Magnetic field magnitude
description: Essential: Correctly calculates B₁ = (5/R)√(mU/e) or equivalent, using the geometry and force balance.

title: Time in magnetic field
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the time in region I as t = (πR√(meU))/(4eU) or equivalent, using the central angle and period.

title: Final kinetic energy
description: Essential: Correctly determines the kinetic energy at emission as E_k = 8eU, based on the number of accelerations.

title: Maximum initial energy coefficient
description: Essential: Correctly solves for the maximum k = 13/6, ensuring the electron does not collide with the outer boundary.

title: Geometry of magnetic motion
description: Important: Applies the given geometry (tan 22.5° = 0.4) to find the trajectory radius r₁ = 0.4R in region I.

title: Force balance in magnetic field
description: Important: Uses Lorentz force as centripetal force (evB = mv²/r) correctly for calculations in magnetic regions.

title: Work-energy theorem application
description: Important: Applies the work-energy theorem to relate kinetic energy changes to electric potential (e.g., 2eU = ½mv₁² for first acceleration).

title: Collision condition geometry
description: Important: Sets up the geometric condition (√3R - r_m)² = R² + r_m² for the maximum radius to avoid collision in part (4).

title: Sign or direction error
description: Pitfall: Uses an incorrect sign for the electron charge in force or energy equations, or misinterprets field directions.

title: Unit or relativistic oversight
description: Pitfall: Fails to use consistent SI units or inappropriately applies relativistic corrections despite instructions to ignore them.
